subject: The (Shiny) app unexpectedly exited... Where do I look for diagnostic information dumped to console

messages.author: e9ea40ad71e07dc0
messages.subject: The (Shiny) app unexpectedly exited... Where do I look for diagnostic information dumped to console
parts:
I received this warning after recently (screen capture attached), updating by App to use reactiveValues and observeEvent functions. Previously it was working fine, just noting the last difference. 

My question is how do I diagnosis the issue. It says to diagnostic information dumped to JavaScript error console, I'm not sure if I am looking at the right place or barking up the right trees.

Some more info:

I deployed the app to shinyapps.io and it works fine. Also works fine locally. 

I am getting the error when attempting to run on shinyserver running on ubuntu instance on Amazon Web Services.

Not sure but using Chrome, under more tools/java script console/console, I see some packages loading and something about RJSONIO..  

I thought the "unexpectedly exited"might have something to do with RJSONIO which is mentioned in the console and was the last thing it mentioned.


Further Below is a comparison of sessionInfo()'s

Many Thanks to all/any who can help, let me know if there is other info I can provide or check
Mike

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: The (Shiny) app unexpectedly exited... Where do I look for diagnostic information dumped to console
parts:
The comparison of sessionInfo() shows that 1) the R versions are
different; 2) the versions of DT/htmlwidgets/shiny are also different.
So I'd recommended you to update everything on your locale machine,
and see if you can reproduce the error locally. If you can, hopefully
you should see a more informative error in R that tells you what
exactly went wrong.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: e9ea40ad71e07dc0
messages.subject: Re: The (Shiny) app unexpectedly exited... Where do I look for diagnostic information dumped to console
parts:
Thanks Yihui, while updating those packages, something else occurred to me. I went back to what I had changed most recently and I figured it out.

The observeEvent, that I have triggered by a reactive function doesn't seem to work the same on shinyapps.io and locally vs. shinyserver on AWS.

My code shown below and a general gist of what I am trying to do is: 

I have an "EditInventory" that is a table of program inventories that I want to default load as initial Inventory table if the Login() changes from False to True. Action buttons control updates to the Edit version of the table from various sources.

The bold blue code below works as expected for me locally and on shinyapps.io, but would not work running on shinyserver on amazon. I am guessing that it has something to do with the order of execution of reactive functions (?). I commented it out and it works on AWS running shinyserver.

After all this I tried another work around I tried (and unexpectedly didn't work):

EditInventory<-reactiveValues(data=Inventory())

I expected that to set the initial value of data of Edit Inventory, but that doesn't work, gives this error

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)



Edit Inventory gets updated various ways in response to different button clicks:

EditInventory<-reactiveValues()

observeEvent(login(), {
  EditInventory$data <- Inventory()})


observeEvent(input$csvinventory, {
  EditInventory$data <- Inventorycsv()})


observeEvent(input$loadeditinventory,{

... 

})



My crude passwording protection:


login<-reactive({
  login<-FALSE
  if (input$submitpasskey[1]==0){return}
  if (input$submitpasskey[1]>0){
    isolate({
      
      if (input$Org=="Bainbridge Island, WA" & input$passkey == "****"){login<-TRUE}
    ...
      
      return(login)
    })
  }
})


Loads an initial Inventory:

Inventory<-reactive({
  if (input$submitpasskey[1]>0){
  if (login()==FALSE){Inventory<-NULL
  return()}
  if (login()==TRUE){
    
    inventorydb<-CPBB_CityData()[CPBB_CityData()$CPBBID==LoginCPBBID(),"CPBBShort"]
    inventorydb<-paste(inventorydb,"inventory",sep='')
    
    if (input$loadinventory[1]==0){
    con <- dbConnect(MySQL(),

...

})


(lastly - if anyone is still listening, please see my other post and any help on how I can get the prettier version of shinydashboard back :) )

Thanks
Mike
